question: In foreign technology agreements, automatic permission is provided in high priority industry up to a sum of __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1 crore**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the** New Industrial Policy of 199**1, automatic permission is provided in high priority industries for foreign technology **agreements up to a sum of Rs. 1 crore. **
 
• This means that companies operating in** high priority sectors can automatically enter into foreign technolog**y agreements without needing additional government approval as long as the total payment for technology transfer does not exceed Rs. 1 crore. 
 
• This** helps streamline the process**, encouraging foreign investment and technology transfer into sectors that are crucial for the nation's development.
 
• For **amounts exceeding ₹1 crore, **companies would need to obtain approval from the government or appropriate authorities.
 
• This policy** aims to balance ease of doing business with oversight to ensure national interests are maintained.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **New Industrial Policy (NIP) of 1991 **was a reform program that aimed to liberalize the Indian economy and increase the competitiveness of its industries.
 
• The **policy was a response to a balance of payments cris**is. 
 
• **Objectives** 
 
 
• **Liberalization**: Reduce government control and increase the role of the private sector
 
• **Privatization: **Increase the role of the private sector in industrial development
 
• **Globalization: **Integrate the Indian economy with the world economy
